Data Quality (DQ) Issue:
Timestamp discrepancy between subscription activation
 and payment processing
Technical Impact:
I set a 2-hour threshold for timestamp discrepancies to account for standard batch sync intervals and provider retry delays, regardless of whether activation occurs on the same day or across days.


This delay can be caused by several factors:
1. Webhook & API Failures: System failed to capture incoming webhook events or API updates.
2. System Infrastructure Delays: Heavy system load and high resource utilization delayed processing pipelines.
Business Impact:
1. 60 subscriptions (41.96% of 143) were activated within 2 hours of payment (including both same-day activations and late payments).

2. 47 subscriptions (32.87% of 143) were activated more than 2 hours after payment.

3. 18 subscriptions (12.59% of 143) experienced both delayed activation and late payments.

Creates a poor user experience due to delayed activation, leading users to cancel their plans.
Suggestion:
1. Create a dbt level 2 (L2) test  to detect and alert on timestamp discrepancies.

2. Add 3 new columns to model activation timing:

    a. start_date_diff: Calculates the timestamp difference between payment and activation.

    b. activation_speed: Categorizes the activation sequence:

        i. same_day_activate: Payment and activation occur on the same date.
        ii. cross_day_activate: Subscription is activated the day after payment is completed.
        iii. late_payment: Payment occurs after the subscription is already activated.

    c. activation_timeliness: Evaluates the delay against the 2-hour SLA window:

        i. reasonable_timeline: Time difference is within the 2-hour threshold.
        ii. late_activation: Time difference exceeds the 2-hour threshold.

3. Propose collaborating with the payment provider on a permanent solution while improving internal system ingestion.
